t: Cycene Restaurant Shoreditch, London Review: Sublime Michelin-star dining with foraged finds
s: November 3, 2025 - A frozen-raspberry accessorised oyster comes in a wooden box that could be a coffin for a particularly loved gerbil, and one of many puddings comes laced with crispy artichoke slivers. The detail is tremendous, the flavours even more so. Cycene might not be the more affordable restaurant in east London, but it is by far the most magical.

t: Cycene, the High Style New Restaurant at London's hip Blue Mountain School
s: December 2, 2022 - But it’s a place of learning nonetheless: The six-story brick hub in Shoreditch showcases a concise, highbrow mix of fashion, art, and craft. It also has a restaurant tucked into the second floor: the Michelin-starred Mãos just reopened as Cycene, remodeled dining room and enlarged kitchen included.

t: review of British restaurant Cycene in Shoreditch by Andy Hayler in November 2022
s: Cycene (“kitchen” in old English) opened in Shoreditch in late October 2022 on the site of what was previously Maos. It is in a building called the Blue Mountain School, in which seemingly “fashion, food, and design combine to achieve a new, esoteric extreme in high-end retail." Er, OK then.

t: Restaurant Review: Cycene London is Redefining Fine Dining
s: March 23, 2023 - While virtually all decent restaurants offer a wine pairing and some very good ones will have a non-alcoholic alternative, Cycene takes things one step further with a ‘half-and-half’ option, where glasses of fine wine are alternated with homemade kombuchas.

t: Cycene (*) - London, England - Dining and Cooking
s: March 22, 2025 - There's no getting around it: the Blue Mountain School in Shoreditch has been something of a revolving door for restaurants and chefs alike over the last few years. The site opened in 2018 and initially hosted the one-Michelin star Mãos. Once that restaurant shuttered, Cycene opened in 2022 under Theo Clench (who has worked at Trinity, Clove Club, Portland, and Akoko), and was awarded one Michelin star six months later.

t: Cycene restaurant review: London is all the better for it
s: With his fingerprints at Cycene, the usual hallmarks of serious eating are all there to see: your server will lovingly tell you about the provenance of the oyster from Carlingford; the sommelier will delight at the pinot noir they’ll pair with your segment of duck, a Stabilo-sized cut of the bird that’s been roasted on the crown to a flush of pink, singing with the flavours of time, game and fire; there’ll be an ageing chamber, clay beakers, and plum ingredients you’d likely find in the Ducasse portfolio, as with the cavatelli that’s been tossed around with uni and dusted with thin shingles of truffle.
